13 accessory ideas

Base cabinets

Wide-unit pull-out shelves

Kabbie says

Give your everyday pots and pans a shelf that comes to you. Slide out the tray and pick what you need without reaching into the back.

Try this organizing tip

Keep your most-used pan near the front and group lids beside their matching pots. Each tray belongs inside one cabinet compartment: try cooking tools on one side and baking pieces on the other.

Base cabinets

Wide-unit drawer organizers

Kabbie says

Let’s give each kitchen tool its own little home. Separate cutlery, serving spoons and measuring tools inside the upper drawer.

Try this organizing tip

Group measuring spoons with measuring cups, and keep serving pieces in their own section. Check the insert against each drawer’s usable interior, rather than the full cabinet width.

Base cabinets

Under-sink pull-out

Kabbie says

Sponges, dish soap and cleaning cloths can be easier to find. A pull-out brings your cleaning supplies forward instead of leaving them hidden behind the sink.

Try this organizing tip

Keep daily dishwashing supplies together and leave space around the pipes. Store cleaning chemicals securely away from children and follow their labels; this organizer is not a child-safety lock.

Base cabinets · Tall / pantry

Roll-out shelves

Kabbie says

No more moving three pots to find the one at the back. Pull the shelf forward to see your cookware, mixing bowls or small kitchen appliances.

Try this organizing tip

Give everyday cookware the easiest-to-reach tray. Keep heavier pieces low and avoid tall stacks that make putting things away harder.

Base cabinets

Utensil dividers

Kabbie says

Whisks, spatulas and measuring spoons do not need to share a jumble. Dividers help you spot the right tool and return it to the same place.

Try this organizing tip

Sort by what you do: prep tools together, baking tools together and serving pieces together. Leave a little extra room so nothing catches when the drawer closes.

Base cabinets

Spice pull-out

Kabbie says

Keep your favorite flavors close to the cooking action. A narrow pull-out brings spice jars into view instead of hiding them in rows.

Try this organizing tip

Group spices by how you cook, with everyday favorites easiest to reach. Keep heat-sensitive ingredients away from direct heat and check jar heights before choosing the rack.

Base cabinets

Trash & recycling pull-out

Kabbie says

Keep the cleanup corner looking tidy. Pull the bins out when you need them, then tuck trash and recycling behind the cabinet front.

Try this organizing tip

Use one bin for trash and another for your household’s recycling routine. Keep spare liners nearby and check that the bins lift out easily for cleaning.

Base cabinets

Corner organizer

Kabbie says

Let’s make that awkward corner easier to use. An organizer can bring suitable pots, bowls or food containers toward the cabinet opening.

Try this organizing tip

Choose items you can lift comfortably and leave enough space for the mechanism to move. Corners vary, so match the organizer to your cabinet before planning what goes inside.

Tall / pantry

Pantry pull-outs

Kabbie says

Give groceries a clear place to live. Pull-out pantry shelves help you see jars, cans and snack containers without searching behind the front row.

Try this organizing tip

Group breakfast, baking and snacks into zones. Put newer items behind older ones and keep heavier groceries on lower shelves within comfortable reach.

Wall cabinets

Shelf riser

Kabbie says

A small riser can separate mugs from little plates and make the shelf easier to scan. It sits on the shelf your cabinet already has.

Try this organizing tip

Try mugs underneath and small plates above, leaving room to lift both out comfortably. The riser is an extra organizer; the cabinet shelf itself is included.

Wall cabinets

Tray & board dividers

Kabbie says

Give cutting boards and compact baking trays a place to stand. You can choose one without lifting the whole stack.

Try this organizing tip

Arrange pieces by size and keep everyday items near the opening. Choose light pieces that fit the shallow cabinet and leave enough room above to lift them out.

Wall cabinets

Corner turntable

Kabbie says

Bring small jars or mugs around to you with a gentle turn. A rotating tray helps you see what is tucked into a wall-cabinet corner.

Try this organizing tip

Keep shorter, lighter pieces around the edge and leave room for a full turn. Check that the tray and its contents clear the doors when they close.

Tall / pantry

Storage baskets & caddies

Kabbie says

Give household essentials their own grab-and-go basket. Group linens, cloths or supplies so you can take out the set you need.

Try this organizing tip

Make one caddy for each routine, such as cleaning cloths or spare tea towels. Keep the loaded basket light enough to carry and avoid mixing food with cleaning chemicals.
